headline: Highest risk is medium: PaddleOCR can ingest documents/images and call APIs, while mem0 stores memory with no documented isolation, creating leakage and workflow-conflict paths; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: mem0 has no documented shared channel or parser surface, while PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can call APIs. The pair lacks evidence of direct instruction ingestion, so only an unusual copy-paste or file handoff path is plausible. Uncertainty keeps this above none, but the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is manually copied into mem0 as instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared file or clipboard bridge, attacker text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable manual copy-paste of untrusted OCR output into mem0.
Add a review step before mem0 stores any OCR-derived text.
Use a provenance tag for OCR outputs.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization before memory ingestion.

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images and can call APIs, while mem0 is a knowledge-management system with no stated isolation or data-class limits. A shared workspace or handoff could move sensitive document content into mem0 and onward through PaddleOCR's API calls. The interaction is plausible in default workflows, so medium fits.
conditions: IF documents or images processed by PaddleOCR contain sensitive data, leakage risk increases.
IF mem0 stores OCR-derived text in the same workspace, both agents can access the same content.
IF PaddleOCR sends extracted content to external APIs, data leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate directories.
Redact sensitive fields before OCR.
Disable API calls for sensitive documents.
Review stored mem0 entries for document-derived secrets.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR has allowlisted network egress and browser execution, while mem0 is a memory service with no concurrency or locking details. Their write surfaces are not explicit, but both can participate in the same workflow and mutate shared artifacts indirectly. Because locking is undocumented, conflict risk is plausible and should be treated as medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared document or index, last-writer conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator routes both agents to the same mutable resource without locks, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output paths.
Serialize writes through one orchestrator step.
Turn off browser automation when not needed.
Use file-level locking for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks on shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR can produce extracted text from documents/images, and mem0 is a memory system that may store or reuse that output. If mem0 treats OCR text as authoritative, downstream decisions can propagate OCR mistakes without verification. The pair lacks evidence of built-in validation, so the cascade is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF mem0 stores OCR output without human review, errors can persist and recur.
IF downstream automation consumes mem0 entries as facts, OCR mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review before storing OCR results.
Mark OCR-derived entries as untrusted.
Compare OCR output against source images for critical fields.
Limit downstream actions to read-only summaries.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR explicitly touches documents and images and can call APIs, while mem0 is a memory store with no documented residency or retention controls. No specific regulated data class or jurisdiction mismatch is shown, so compliance risk is limited to policy gaps rather than a proven breach. The other agent is not cited because no residency or certification data is provided.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through PaddleOCR APIs, retention and residency policies must be checked.
IF mem0 stores the same documents without a deletion policy, retention mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair.
Set a short retention window for stored OCR text.
Delete OCR artifacts after use.
Review vendor terms for residency and retention.
requires-engineering: implement jurisdiction-aware routing.
